description: ASTRA-MED Orbital Health is a physician-led project exploring AI-assisted health monitoring for astronauts during long-duration space missions. Our goal is to develop a prototype that integrates physiological data, risk detection, and clinical decision support. We welcome collaborators interested in software engineering, AI/ML, data science, and space medicine. Our focus is clinically informed, practical, and transparent about the prototype's limitations.
summary:
ASTRA-MED Orbital Health is a browser-based research prototype for astronaut health awareness during long-duration space missions.

The application uses synthetic data from three fictional crew scenarios, each covering twelve mission days. It displays resting heart rate, oxygen saturation, sleep duration, and self-reported strain through interactive visualizations.

Users can select a scenario and mission day, review physiological trends, and run an illustrative assessment based on transparent rules. The software then displays a non-diagnostic status and suggestions for human review.

The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG. It works locally without external services.

NASA's Human Research Program resources informed the project's focus on the challenges of spaceflight and crew autonomy.

ChatGPT assisted with code generation, interface development, documentation, and presentation preparation.

All measurements are fictional. The alert thresholds are not clinically validated. The software does not use real astronaut medical data, connected sensors, or a trained machine-learning model. It is not suitable for diagnosis or operational spaceflight use.

Future development would involve validated biomedical data, sensor integration, aerospace medicine collaboration, and clinical safety testing.

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and SVG, it displays synthetic physiological data across three fictional crew scenarios and twelve mission days. Users can examine heart rate, oxygen saturation, sleep duration, and self-reported strain.

The software provides interactive trend charts and transparent rule-based alerts intended to demonstrate how astronauts could identify concerning changes and request human medical review.

NASA Human Research Program resources informed the project's design. ChatGPT assisted with coding, documentation, and presentation development.

All data are synthetic, and the alerts are illustrative rather than clinically validated. The prototype does not contain a trained AI model and is not intended for medical diagnosis or operational use.
